svg.text: Veroboard (stripboard) layout: ADS1115 sender interface, no track cuts

Component side, copper strips shown through the board. 20 strips × 24 holes (about 61 × 51 mm), cut from a standard 0.1 in stripboard. Built from hardware/WIRING.md and wiring.svg; checked against the schematic before drawing.
J2-1: ground-sense wire (to the tank stud)
J2-2: sender signal wire (to the spade)
J3 5 V in: car only, later (see notes)
pins col 9, strips 9–18 (VDD … A3), body to the right
strip 19 ground sense, strip 20 sender, col 23
No track cuts: every strip is one connection end to end.
Spans of 2 strips (R1, R2, R4): use 0.125 W resistors to lie flat.
Strips 3, 4, 5 (GPIO16, RX, TX) and 8 (5 V) belong to the
display: nothing else may touch them. Strip 8 is live (USB 5 V).
Strip 14 carries only the module's ALRT pin.
A2 is unused and tied to 3.3 V (TI allows unused inputs at VDD),
so its strip doubles as the 3.3 V strip for Rp, R1 and R4.
Measurement taps sit beyond each load, outside the current path:
3.3 V enters strip 17 at col 21, so R1 (col 3) is past Rp;
R2 and R3 sit left of Rp and R4, away from J2.
Caps sit on the ADS1115 side of their 1 kΩ, as in WIRING.md.
Input protection for the car is not shown yet (WIRING.md).
1. Inspect for solder bridges, especially strips 6–7–8–9.
2. Meter, unpowered: no continuity between strips except
3. Offer the board up to the case: strip 1 must meet the
socket labelled 18 and strip 8 the socket labelled 5V.
4. Power up: strip 6 ≈ 3.3 V and strip 8 ≈ 5 V; nothing else.
Links (insulated wire on the component side)
Parts lie flat across the strips they join; the body sits on the component side and touches nothing in between. Keep everything low if the board will sit against the back of the case.

J1: male header that plugs into the display's sockets; the board can then be screwed or clipped to the case so the header cannot work loose. J2: use a latching 2.54 mm connector (for example Molex KK 254).

J3 (dashed): only for the car, to feed the display from a 12 V → 5 V automotive converter through its 5V socket. Check the board's power path first (WIRING.md), and never connect USB at the same time.
